Permutations that move the patches of biogeographic events

Source: R/patches.R
patch_permutations.Rd

A restricted null model for the events of node_test() in landscapes with edges, such as refugia in a biome or islands in an archipelago. Each area is split into patches of neighbouring sites. In each permutation, every patch is placed around a site drawn at random, on the sites nearest to it that are still free, from the smallest patch to the largest. The number and size of the patches are kept, and so is the fact that sites of a patch are neighbours, while their place changes. Permutations of a torus cannot do this, because a landscape with edges does not wrap around.

Usage

patch_permutations(coords, biogeography, n_perm = 999, gap = NULL)

Arguments

coords

Matrix or data frame with the two coordinates of each site, in the order of the rows of biogeography.

biogeography

Matrix of biogeographic events with one row per site and values of 1, -1 and 0, as given to node_test().

n_perm

Number of permutations.

gap

Largest distance between neighbouring sites of a patch. The default, 1.5 times the median distance to the nearest site, joins diagonal neighbours in a regular grid.

Value

List with one integer matrix per event, each with one permutation per row and the names of the sites as column names, for area_permutations in node_test(). Rows only move the areas of that event, so they should not be used as site_permutations.

Details

Patches take a compact form near their random site, so their shape is not kept, and a patch next to an edge or to another patch may take an elongated form or be split. Distances are Euclidean, so coordinates should be projected. A landscape with holes or with parts far apart, such as islands, may give patches that cross the gaps.

This method was built for this package and has no published evaluation. In data-raw/validation_edges.R, with communities that followed a hidden autocorrelated environment and areas without effect, it rejected 3.0% to 6.3% of the tests at the 5% level in a square, a strip and an irregular band, against 44% to 55% with free permutations (see the article on analysing clades). Autocorrelation at a scale close to that of the landscape, areas much larger than those simulated and real landscapes were not evaluated.

See also

torus_permutations() for a torus. biogeography_matrix() codes the events.

Examples

coords <- expand.grid(x = 1:10, y = 1:6)
event <- ifelse(coords$x <= 3 & coords$y <= 3, 1, ifelse(coords$x >= 8, -1, 0))
permutations <- patch_permutations(coords, cbind(barrier = event), n_perm = 3)

# where the first permutation places the two sides
matrix(event[permutations$barrier[1, ]], 10)
#>       [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6]
#>  [1,]    0    0    0    0    0    0
#>  [2,]    0    0    0   -1   -1    0
#>  [3,]    0   -1   -1   -1   -1   -1
#>  [4,]    0   -1   -1   -1   -1   -1
#>  [5,]    0   -1   -1   -1   -1    0
#>  [6,]    0    0   -1   -1    0    0
#>  [7,]    0    0    1    1    1    0
#>  [8,]    0    0    1    1    1    0
#>  [9,]    0    0    1    1    1    0
#> [10,]    0    0    0    0    0    0
